open_points.subject: EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS
open_points.text: “the conclusion each NodeExecution status gives (A13 rules 5 and 7) … is a correspondence over that taxonomy … whose cells name members”
open_points.question: Which model enumeration represents an execution conclusion, and what exact member does each NodeExecution status map to?
options: Add a closed execution-conclusion enumeration and specify the complete status-to-conclusion table
Use existing NodeExecution statuses as conclusions and specify which statuses collapse together
Represent conclusions as structured values rather than enumeration members
open_points.default_guess: Add a closed conclusion enumeration such as succeeded, failed, waiting, skipped and refused, then state every table row explicitly.

open_points.subject: outcome_unknown execution conclusion
open_points.question: How can a total table keyed only by NodeExecution status represent `outcome_unknown`, whose conclusion changes with the EffectAttempt resolution and whether the binding has output ports under A11 rule 3?
options: Exclude operation statuses requiring EffectAttempt context from this table and continue obtaining their conclusions from effects.operation_element_conclusion
Key the table by NodeExecution status plus EffectAttempt status and binding-output presence
Give outcome_unknown a fixed table value and apply a separately specified override
open_points.default_guess: Keep contextual operation conclusions in effects.operation_element_conclusion and restrict the static table to statuses whose conclusions are context-free.

open_points.subject: NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS
open_points.text: “what each node conclusion means for the run and for its dependants … is a correspondence over that taxonomy … whose cells name members”
open_points.question: What is the row taxonomy and exact cell shape of NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS, given that the models define neither a NodeConclusion enumeration nor enumerations for the two independent results—run treatment and dependant treatment?
options: Introduce model enumerations for node conclusions, run treatment and dependant treatment, with one row containing both effects
Key directly by NodeExecution status and use a structured cell containing run and dependant effects
Split it into separate total tables for run treatment and dependant treatment
open_points.default_guess: Introduce explicit conclusion and effect enumerations and make each row contain separate run and dependant effects.

open_points.subject: HTTP_METHOD_BODIES
open_points.text: “whether an HTTP method carries a body … is a correspondence over that taxonomy … whose cells name members”
open_points.question: What model member does each HTTP_METHOD_BODIES cell name, since models has an HTTP-method enumeration but no body-policy enumeration and the rule otherwise appears Boolean?
options: Add a body-policy enumeration with body and no_body members
Define the table values as booleans, making the ‘cells name members’ statement inapplicable here
Map methods to an existing request-body representation type
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed body-policy enumeration with body for POST, PUT and PATCH and no_body for GET and DELETE.
